slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A proof about angles chains together definitions and theorems: linear pairs are supplementary, vertical angles are equal, complements and supplements of the same angle are equal, and the angle addition postulate.

Example: Given angle 1 and angle 2 are vertical angles and m angle 1 = 3x + 10, m angle 2 = 5x − 30. Then 3x + 10 = 5x − 30 (vertical angles are equal), so 40 = 2x and x = 20, giving each angle 70 degrees. A flow chart proof shows the same steps as boxes with arrows, each box labeled with its reason.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Angles 1 and 2 form a linear pair, with m angle 1 = 2x and m angle 2 = 4x. Find x.
slides.reveal: 2x + 4x = 180, so 6x = 180 and x = 30 (the angles are 60 and 120 degrees).
